messages:
lina_sec: :rotating_light: Observed a concentrated traffic surge from ASN 395987 targeting /v1/generate at the edge. WAF rule group 14 triggered & rate limiter hit. Error budget ticking up, 503s from proxy. Starting containment — please ack and standby.

mike_sre: ACK. Pulling recent edge metrics and flow logs. Any signs of new customer traffic patterns or recent config changes?

lina_sec: No config changes in last 6h. IDS shows repeated identical payload shapes + fast retry loops. Likely botnet/probing.

anya_prod: We're seeing user-facing errors for a few customers in NA region. Not widespread yet but growth is steep. Posting snippet of request headers and counts: 
```
SrcASN: 395987, UA: okhttp/4.9.3, path: /v1/generate, qps: 820 -> 4xx/5xx ratio rising
```

jordan_enginfra: I can push an emergency WAF rule to block ASN 395987 and add aggressive rate-limit on /v1/generate. Anyone object? Also we should lock down who can edit WAF rules — we had a recent RBAC change pending but not deployed.

sam_support: Support informed affected customers with temporary message. Ticket numbers: #5482, #5484. They're asking for ETA.

mike_sre: Do the WAF block + rate-limit. Configure rate-limit header so legitimate retries can see Retry-After. Also enable prefix KV caching bypass to avoid cache poisoning.

jordan_enginfra: Pushing rule now. Command: 
```
# apply temporary block
rctl waf apply --block-asn 395987 --path '/v1/generate' --reason 'emergency traffic abuse 1815432100'
```
deploy-bot: WAF change queued by jordan_enginfra at 1815432154, change-id: wafchg-7731. Rolling to edges.

jordan_enginfra: Change applied to 85% of POPs, tuning to 100%. Observed drop in qps from ASN 395987 -> 92%. 503s trending down.

lina_sec: Great. Next: audit trail & compliance. Audit-bot, ensure the WAF change and any key usage are logged to the audit stream, and snapshot KMS key usage for the last 24 hours.

audit-bot: Audit logs for wafchg-7731 recorded. KMS access summary (last 24h): 12 decrypts for model checkpoints (service accounts: model-serving), 3 key-rotate ops (system), 0 suspicious access patterns. Full export available at https://internal.redwood/audit/exports/1815432100.csv

mike_sre: Thanks. One follow-up: who currently has write RBAC to WAF and edge routing? We should tighten permissions to a small oncall group until we finish triage.

jordan_enginfra: Current policy: group=edge-admins (6 people) and infra-sre (3 people). I propose temporary policy edge-emergency (2 people: jordan_enginfra, mike_sre) with timebound 4h sudo. I'll open the RBAC change.

lina_sec: Do it. Make change auditable and include justification. I'll add a compliance note for incident record.

jordan_enginfra: Executing RBAC change: 
```
rbacctl apply --grant edge-emergency --members jordan_enginfra,mike_sre --expires 4h --scope waf,edge-routing --reason 'emergency DDoS containment 1815432100'
```
rbacctl: policy-update: success (op-id rbacop-4412)

mike_sre: Confirmed. Only jordan and I can edit WAF now. Also toggled stricter log retention for edge flow logs + pushed them to long-term S3 for post-incident forensics.

anya_prod: Support updated customers with ETA ~2h and mitigation steps. All verbal escalations routed to oncall.

lina_sec: Good. Action items for post-incident: 1) Revert temporary RBAC after review, 2) Add ASN 395987 to permanent watchlist, 3) Create WAF rule template that limits collateral for small customers, 4) Review KMS key access patterns and rotate any keys if needed, 5) Run vuln triage on any edge libs that had high error rates.

sam_support: I'll own customer comms postmortem.

mike_sre: I'll own forensic export + run retrospective on rate-limit thresholds. Jordan, handoff RBAC revert to infra team after 24h.

jordan_enginfra: Will file PR for long-term RBAC policy and doc steps. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/532

audit-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-0319-81. Audit bundle: https://internal.redwood/audit/bundles/INC-2026-0319-81.zip

lina_sec: OK wrapping: traffic down ~95% from peak, WAF block holding, no sign of data plane compromise. Leave this thread open for any follow-ups. Great job team. :thumbsup:

mike_sre: +1. I'll update oncall handoff in 30m.

jordan_enginfra: Reverting temporary rate-limit after 4h window unless we detect resurgence.

sam_support: Closing affected tickets after postmortem comms.

lina_sec: Closing note: schedule a tabletop to review RBAC cadence and KMS access controls next week.

(END)
